english.title: Subject of a debt relief order under the Insolvency Act 1986 dispose of property during prohibited period

a

english.legislation: Contrary to section 251Q(1), 251T(3) and 430 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) The reference in subsection (1) to making a transfer of any property includes causing or conniving at the levying of any execution against that property - section 251Q(2)
(ii) A person is not guilty of the offence under this section if he provs that, in respect of the conduct constituting the offence, he had no intent to defraud or to conceal the state of his affairs - section 251Q(3)
(iii) For the purposes of subsection (3) a person is to be taken to have proved that he had no such intent if-
(a) sufficient evidence is adduced to raise an issue as to whether he had such intent; and (b) the contrary is not proved beyond reasonable doubt - section 251Q(4)
(iv) It is immaterial for the purposes of this section whether or not the debt relief order in question is revoked after the conduct constituting an offence takes place (but no offence is committed by virtue of conduct occurring after the order is revoked) - section 251Q(5)
(v) This offence was Inserted by section 108(1) of and Schedule 17 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (limit on magistrates' court powers to impose imprisonment), the reference to "twelve months" is to be read as a reference to "six months".

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
